title: Architecture Evolution, Economics, and Organization

weeks.focus: Model and freeze change coupling, candidate boundaries, ownership, sourcing, and economics
Build compatibility, cost, backfill, shadowing, cutover, and rollback controls
Break and measure nine migration, economic, dependency, and ownership controls
Decide, teach, assess, and remediate the technical strategy

readiness_note: Draft until deterministic lab, six-run calibration, semantic review, resource verification, and focused and full validation pass.

outcomes.statement: Select modular-monolith, service, or event boundaries from change, workload, failure, data-authority, security, and ownership evidence.
Model Conway effects, interaction cost, cognitive load, ownership, and succession for an evolving architecture.
Compare managed, open-source, custom, and platform choices with explicit operating, security, governance, portability, and exit obligations.
Calculate fully loaded cost and cost per useful outcome with allocation, sensitivity, and stopping thresholds.
Design compatibility policies and expand-and-contract changes for mixed-version operation.
Implement resumable backfills, shadow comparison, controlled cutover, rollback, and evidence-based decommissioning.
Diagnose nine evolution failures without losing authority, data, service, cost control, dependency control, or ownership continuity.
Defend a multi-quarter strategy with outcomes, sequencing, staffing, dependencies, dissent, stopping conditions, and reversal evidence.

resources.title: Under Deconstruction: The State of Shopify's Monolith
resources.purpose: Compare modularization with service extraction using observed change and complexity costs.
resources.assignment: Read the complete article; record three boundary drivers, two reasons to remain modular, and one extraction threshold.

resources.title: Conway's Law and How Do Committees Invent?
resources.purpose: Connect communication paths to interface structure without treating organization as destiny.
resources.assignment: Read the author page and linked original paper; map three required technical interfaces to their human communication paths.

resources.title: Team Interaction Modeling with Team Topologies
resources.purpose: Make cognitive load, ownership, and temporary versus durable interactions visible.
resources.assignment: Read the interaction-modeling and cognitive-load sections; draw current and target interaction maps with one expiry condition.

resources.title: Capability: Unit Economics
resources.purpose: Connect technical spend to a useful product outcome and decision threshold.
resources.assignment: Read Definition, Functional Activities, and Inputs and Outputs; define one business unit metric, one resource metric, sources, owner, and threshold.

resources.title: Patterns of Legacy Displacement
resources.author_or_publisher: Ian Cartwright, Rob Horn, and James Lewis; MartinFowler.com
resources.purpose: Design incremental seams and transitional architecture tied to outcomes and removal conditions.
resources.assignment: Read Breaking the Cycle, Successfully Deliver the Parts, and the middleware example; produce a seam, transition asset, removal condition, and cost-of-risk argument.

resources.title: Online Migrations at Scale
resources.purpose: Examine phased writes, backfill, comparison, cutover, and cleanup in a live migration.
resources.assignment: Read the complete article; identify authority in each phase, backfill verification, divergence risk, cutover gate, and cleanup proof.

resources.title: Semantic Versioning 2.0.0
resources.purpose: Use a declared public contract and explicit compatibility signal while recognizing limits for data and protocols.
resources.assignment: Read the Summary and specification items 1-11; classify six changes and state two cases where SemVer cannot prove runtime compatibility.

resources.title: Canarying Releases
resources.purpose: Bound blast radius and connect promotion or rollback to measured candidate-versus-control evidence.
resources.assignment: Read Canary Release through Canary Implementation; define population, duration, comparison metrics, budget exposure, promotion, and rollback thresholds.

resources.title: Maintaining Client Transparency While Migrating Systems
resources.type: recorded practitioner interview with HTML transcript
resources.purpose: Treat traffic replay, discrepancy measurement, gradual cutover, and fast rollback as client-transparency controls.
resources.assignment: Listen to the episode or read the transcript; enumerate user-visible states, mismatch measures, rollout stages, rollback trigger, and one unknown not captured server-side.

failure_experiments.evidence: producer/consumer versions, accepted fields, compatibility decision, rejected event, rollout state, and I03

failure_experiments.scenario: destructive schema contraction while an old reader remains
failure_experiments.evidence: schema phase, reader inventory, deprecation window, contraction decision, rollback, and I04

failure_experiments.scenario: partial backfill restart skips or duplicates records
failure_experiments.evidence: cursor, batch identity, idempotency, counts, reconciliation, restart result, and I05
source of truth, write attempts, versions, divergence, repair path, and I06

failure_experiments.scenario: shadow mismatch is ignored during promotion
failure_experiments.evidence: sample size, normalized mismatch, threshold, promotion decision, owner, and I07
cutover phase, new writes, reverse path, data loss, stop condition, and I08

failure_experiments.scenario: fourfold cost spike is hidden by incomplete allocation
failure_experiments.evidence: direct/shared/labor/transition cost, good outcomes, unit cost, budget, stop decision, and I09

failure_experiments.scenario: managed dependency quota or price change has no executable exit
failure_experiments.evidence: dependency limit, price, portable contract/data, replacement lead time, owner, and I10

failure_experiments.scenario: loss of the primary owning team leaves a critical capability unowned
failure_experiments.evidence: primary/secondary owners, runbook verification, access, escalation, handoff trial, and I11
